title: Multi-policy reset executor for hybrid windowed and rate-limited quota anchors
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood currently has multiple code paths and cron jobs handling quota resets: calendar-aligned monthly/daily resets, rolling-window accumulators for rate-limits, and reserved-capacity lease windows. In edge cases (DST, timezone migrations, clock drift, cross-region reconciliation) tenants have seen transient double-counting or missed resets leading to incorrect usage accounting and billing disputes.

Goal:
Introduce a single, pluggable 'Multi-policy Reset Executor' (MRE) in the quota service that can execute reset policies atomically and idempotently across different quota semantics: calendar-aligned anchors, sliding/rolling windows, and reserved-capacity leases. MRE must provide auditable checkpoints, lease-based fencing to avoid concurrent resets, and a reconciliation mode for historical correction.

Non-goals:
- Replacing tenant billing calculators (billing pipeline remains unchanged)
- Implementing full customer-facing UI in this ticket (console hooks will be a follow-up)

Key requirements:
- Support policy types: calendar (UTC/localized), rolling-window (sliding), lease-window (reserved capacity), and hybrid (e.g., monthly base + intra-month burst bucket).
- Idempotent execution with op_id / checkpoint ledger so retries or duplicate workers do not double-apply resets.
- Time/fence resiliency: handle clock skew, DST transitions, and leap seconds with explicit 'anchor time' and monotonic delta logic.
- Audit trail: persistent reset records with before/after deltas and reason tags for reconciliation.
- Backfill and reconciliation mode: ability to run a non-destructive dry-run and then apply corrections in batches with memoized invoices/adjustments flagged for Finance review.
- Minimal latency impact on token-serving path; reset executor runs asynchronously but must publish immediate quota delta events for downstream throttlers.

Trade-offs and design decisions:
- Central scheduler vs. distributed per-pool executors: we will implement a centralized coordinator with sharded leader leases per region/pool to simplify global ordering and reconciliation. This reduces complexity at cost of a small cross-pool RPC hop.
- Lease-based fencing uses existing leader election/lease service (etcd-backed) rather than new consensus primitives to accelerate rollout.
- Persistent reset ledger stored in the quota DB (append-only table) to simplify joins for billing and audits. This increases DB write volume; mitigation: batch writes and compact older records into weekly summaries.

High-level design:
- Policy definition: JSON policy documents (name, type, anchor tz, cadence, grace window, reconciliation window, linked-reservation-id).
- MRE worker: reads pending policy firing windows, claims lease, computes deltas (using snapshot of tenant usage ledger), emits 'quota-reset' events to event bus, persists a checkpoint entry, and triggers reconciliation hooks if there is a drift above threshold.
- Reconciliation job: separate consumer that inspects checkpoint vs. billing ledger and writes correction entries (flagged for finance).

APIs and schema changes:
- New table: quota_reset_checkpoints (id, policy_name, anchor_ts, claimed_by, before_checksum, after_checksum, delta_summary, status, op_id, created_at).
- New admin API: POST /admin/quotas/policies/_simulate (policy, start, end) -> dry-run summary.
- New event: quota.reset_applied {tenant_id, policy_name, anchor_ts, delta_summary, op_id}

Observability/telemetry:
- Dashboards: policy firing rate, average execution latency, percent of reconciliations triggered, top tenants by correction amount.
- Alerts: >0.5% tenants with corrections in 24h window OR average mismatch > 2% for a policy cadence.

Migration plan:
1) Deploy MRE in dry-run mode for 1 week on 'non-critical' tenants (engineering/dev wallets). Record deltas but do not apply (status=DRY_RUN).
2) Enable apply mode for a progressively larger percentage: 5% -> 20% -> 100% over two weeks, verifying that correction volume and Finance tickets remain acceptable.
3) Switch reserved-capacity leases to be owned by MRE (coexistence mode: legacy cron still runs but marks leases as migrated once MRE writes first checkpoint).

Rollout safety and revert plan:
- Feature flag gated by region and tenant tier.
- All applied resets include op_id & checkpoint; rollback tool will scan checkpoint entries for op_id and create compensating deltas (also recorded) if we detect systemic errors.

Acceptance criteria:
- MRE can successfully compute and persist a dry-run for both calendar and rolling policies for 1000 tenants in under 15 minutes of wall-clock time in test cluster.
- No additional throttling incidents caused by the executor during rollout in canary region.
- Reconciliation pipeline can propose corrections and Finance can identify corrections via the 'corrections' dashboard.

implementation_notes: Use existing lease manager for per-shard leader claim. Each shard processes a subset of tenant hashes to allow horizontal scaling.
Batch DB writes for checkpoint records and publish aggregated delta summaries to reduce write amplification.
Introduce op_id UUID for all executor runs to make operations idempotent and traceable across retries.
Use monotonic clock (system uptime) to compute deltas where possible to protect against NTP adjustments in host machines.
Compact checkpoint ledger older than 90 days into weekly summaries; keep full audit for 13 months per compliance request.
test_plan: Unit tests for policy parser and anchor timezone handling.
Integration test: dry-run vs legacy cron delta comparison for 10k synthetic tenants.
Load test: MRE should complete shard processing for 5k tenants in under 30 minutes in staging cluster size S2.
Manual Finance review: surface corrections UI for a sample of migrated tenants and validate invoice flags.
Canary rollout on engineering org accounts for 7 days, then gradual increase as per migration plan.
monitoring: grafana: Quota Reset Success Rate by Policy
grafana: Avg execution latency per tenant shard
revert_plan: If systemic mismatch detected (>2% avg delta across tenants), flip feature flag to DRY_RUN immediately.
Run compensating deltas using op_id lookup to reverse applied resets where safe; log reversible ops in recovery ledger.
Open post-mortem and notify Finance + CS for impacted customers and create credit tickets as needed.
